job.style: a market or shop situation that uses the idea

response.passage: Rohan visited a local craft market to buy decorations for his school project. He noticed a beautiful wooden star, which is a regular pentagon shape. The shopkeeper explained that because it is a regular polygon, it has five distinct lines of symmetry, not just one. Rohan then looked at a square-shaped mirror. He held his notebook with the letter 'P' written on it in front of the mirror. He was surprised to see that the reflection showed the letter flipped horizontally, proving that a mirror image is not exactly the same as the original object. Next, he examined a circular clock face. The shopkeeper rotated the clock by 72 degrees, and it looked identical to its starting position, showing it has rotational symmetry of order five. Rohan realized that symmetry is not limited to vertical lines; a shape can have lines of symmetry in any orientation. Finally, he picked up a triangular sign. He learned that a shape has rotational symmetry if it looks the same after a rotation of less than 360 degrees. This trip helped him understand that symmetry is a complex property involving reflections, rotations, and multiple axes of balance.
response.summary: Rohan learns about symmetry by observing regular polygons and reflections at a craft market. He discovers that symmetry involves multiple lines, rotational properties, and mirror reversals.
